description: Matrix multiply: every cell of C is a dot product, the row of A with the column of B, summed over k.

line_docs: The same for every cell at once: the inner product +.× pairs rows of A with columns of B, multiplies, and sums; C receives the whole matrix.
m.purpose: Read right to left: A +.× B is APL's inner product, multiply pairs (×) then add them up (+.), for every row of A against every column of B at once. No i, j or k appears. Placeholder glyphs.
m.title: The same product in the proposed notation

line_docs: Cell (i, j) of C: run k along row i of A and down column j of B, multiply the pairs, add them up.
math.purpose: One line: cell (i, j) of C is the sum over k of A's entry (i, k) times B's entry (k, j). Every cell is a dot product of a row with a column; k is the index they share.
math.title: The product as written on paper

name: matmul

docs: The result: a matrix with as many rows as A and as many columns as B.
Which row of A, and of C.
Which column of B, and of C.
Definition: the left side is computed from the right side.
Add the products up over k: on paper a ∑ over k, in the notation the + of the inner product +.×.
The index the two matrices share: it runs along a row of A and down a column of B, and is summed away. It is the stone's time axis.
The left matrix; its rows are paired with B's columns.
The right matrix; its columns are paired with A's rows.
Multiply the paired entries; written by juxtaposition on the Math face and as the × of +.× in the notation.

title: Matrix multiply

visual.purpose: A and B as grids of cells; at step k the column of A and the row of B that meet are lit, and every cell of C grows by their product, shown as a bar inside the cell.
visual.title: The two matrices and C accumulating
